problem_statement: The accepted Collin source contract identifies a county-specific PACS Access export containing separate current and certified appraisal families, but the exploratory reader did not independently prove exact decoding of its measured 17-byte NUMERIC wrapper and did not resolve a production account identity. This change must define a deterministic, synthetic-only adapter foundation without claiming universal Access compatibility, approving an account key, or introducing acquisition, persistence, orchestration, publication, owner-data, or production-runtime behavior.
desired_outcome: Produce a reviewable OpenSpec delta for an adapter-local Collin decoder foundation that specifies exact Decimal decoding of the measured NUMERIC wrapper, validates the bounded AD_Public projection, creates typed Collin source records, emits distinct immutable current and certified observations with exact provenance, preserves identifiers and physical rows as source facts, uses privacy-safe synthetic fixtures and diagnostics, and remains explicitly non-production until separately accepted implementation and runtime work occurs.
assumptions: The existing collin-cad-source-contract capability is the single capability modified by this source-onboarding change.

The complete D1 through D4 decision-input set is authoritative for drafting because the context manifest includes all four declared parts without truncation; each decision still requires authorized maintainer merge to become accepted.
The implementation boundary can remain within the Collin adapter module, adapter-local tests and fixtures, and directly related source documentation without modifying domain or application contracts.
Issue #43 owns any future production release-processing API, shared vendor-neutral record or provenance abstractions, bounded streaming boundary, and Collin DAG integration.

planning_decisions.decision_text: Support only the measured pure-Python reader's 17-byte NUMERIC wrapper. Byte zero is the canonical sign marker; four little-endian 32-bit magnitude words occur most-significant-word first; external precision and scale metadata control exact Decimal construction. Precision is 1 through 28, scale is 0 through precision, float conversion is prohibited, precision overflow and negative zero fail, and independent literal fixtures cover zero, signed, scaled, multiword, boundary, year, and monetary values.

Validate exactly the AD_Public table and its approved privacy-minimized projection. Bind exact case-sensitive names independently of order; reject duplicate names, ASCII case-fold collisions, missing required structure, and incompatible physical descriptors or nullability. Additional metadata columns are reported but their values are not read. Compute a canonical SHA-256 schema fingerprint as provenance rather than an allowlist.

Represent current and populated certified families as separate immutable adapter-local observations. Current classification comes from property_status; a certified observation is emitted only when cert_val_yr and certified values are consistent. Families never merge, overwrite, relabel, suppress, or fill one another, and each retains family-specific year, source-column lineage, and provenance.

Apply the approved lexical, null-family, identifier, status, year, monetary, exact-Decimal, diagnostic, privacy, task-ordering, and implementation-boundary rules. Diagnostics use the closed stable vocabulary and expose only bounded context. Writes remain limited to the Collin adapter foundation, adapter-local synthetic tests and fixtures, and directly related documentation, while Issue #43-owned production and shared-abstraction areas remain excluded.

boundary: Issue #43 owns the production release-processing API.
Issue #43 owns shared vendor-neutral source-record, provenance, and native-value abstractions.
Issue #43 owns any shared bounded streaming boundary.
Issue #18 must remain a synthetic adapter-local foundation and must not define, modify, or compete with those areas.

task_slices.title: Add independent Collin NUMERIC fixtures
task_slices.description: Add adapter-local reviewed literal fixtures and a provenance/checksum manifest covering canonical zero, positive, negative, scaled, signed multiword, precision-boundary, 2025, 2026, and monetary vectors. Expected literals must not be generated by an encoder or helper mirroring the decoder.
validation_checks: Fixture review confirms literal independence, required vector coverage, checksum documentation, and absence of county or protected data.

task_slices.title: Implement the Collin NUMERIC decoder and structural validator
task_slices.description: Implement the exact Decimal decoder, physical descriptor models, bounded AD_Public projection, descriptor compatibility checks, canonical schema fingerprint, and closed structural diagnostics using the independent fixtures from task 1.1.
validation_checks: Independent vectors decode to reviewed exact Decimal values without float conversion.
Malformed wrapper and incompatible schema cases fail with stable diagnostics before row conversion.
Schema fingerprints are deterministic under descriptor reordering and remain provenance rather than compatibility allowlists.

task_slices.title: Implement typed Collin records and dual observations
task_slices.description: Implement adapter-local typed source records, lexical and null-family validation, exact source-native values, bounded provenance, and separate immutable current and certified observations on top of task 2.1's decoder and structural validation.
validation_checks: Valid synthetic rows produce family-specific current and certified observations with distinct years and lineage.
Invalid identifiers, statuses, years, monetary values, and certified-family combinations fail atomically.
Repeated physical rows and both source identifiers remain preserved without account-key or deduplication claims.

task_slices.title: Add Collin decoder and source-contract tests
task_slices.description: Add positive, negative, schema-drift, exact-value, dual-family, provenance, repeated-row, diagnostic-redaction, privacy, artifact-boundary, and architecture tests for tasks 1.1 through 3.1 without contacting a county source or adding an Access runtime.
validation_checks: Tests cover every D1 through D4 failure class and stable diagnostic vocabulary.
Tests demonstrate atomic failure without partial accepted observations.
Privacy and artifact tests reject owner data, complete source rows, county artifacts, credentials, and host-local paths.
Architecture tests confirm domain, application, services, DAGs, persistence, and deployment remain unchanged.

task_slices.title: Document the Collin Access decoder foundation
task_slices.description: Document the wrapper-specific physical contract, independent fixture provenance, bounded AD_Public projection, dual-roll semantics, unresolved account identity, exact-value and diagnostic behavior, resource assumptions, privacy boundary, Issue #43 boundary, and explicit non-production limitations after task 4.1 establishes the tested behavior.
validation_checks: Documentation links to the normative OpenSpec delta instead of duplicating it and ends with the required related-material navigation.
Documentation does not claim universal Access compatibility, live-release compatibility, or production readiness.

task_slices.title: Run deterministic Collin foundation validation
task_slices.description: Run strict OpenSpec validation and the supported repository documentation, lint, type, test, architecture, artifact-policy, and secret checks after tasks 1.1 through 5.1 complete.

requirements.title: Decode the approved NUMERIC wrapper exactly
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST accept only an exactly 17-byte wrapper with sign byte 0x00 or 0x01 and four little-endian 32-bit magnitude words ordered most-significant-word first, and MUST construct the result directly as an exact Decimal using approved external precision and scale metadata without binary floating-point conversion.

scenarios.name: Decode an independent signed multiword vector
given: an independently authored 17-byte signed multiword fixture
approved precision and scale metadata
a reviewed exact negative Decimal expectation
scenarios.when: the Collin NUMERIC decoder decodes the literal vector without an implementation-derived encoder being involved in the test oracle calculation form; the observable result is the reviewed exact negative Decimal with its declared precision and scale preserved and no float conversion path used.
then: the reviewed exact negative Decimal is returned
the declared precision and scale are preserved
no binary floating-point conversion occurs

requirements.title: Reject unsupported NUMERIC representations
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST reject non-bytes input, widths other than 17 bytes, unsupported sign bytes, missing or invalid precision and scale metadata, precision overflow, negative zero, and malformed non-null numeric values with deterministic stable diagnostics, and MUST NOT convert such values to null, float, or a rounded Decimal.

scenarios.name: Reject a negative-zero wrapper
given: a 17-byte wrapper with sign byte 0x01 and zero magnitude
valid precision and scale metadata
scenarios.when: the Collin NUMERIC decoder validates the wrapper and the observable outcome is a negative_zero failure with no Decimal or partial row record produced.
then: decoding fails with the stable negative_zero diagnostic
no Decimal value or partial row record is returned

requirements.title: Validate the bounded AD_Public schema
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST require exactly the AD_Public table and every approved privacy-minimized column with compatible exact name, physical type, width, precision, scale, and nullability, and MUST fail closed before row conversion for missing or unexpected tables, missing required fields, duplicate names, ASCII case-fold collisions, aliases, renamed fields, or incompatible descriptors.

scenarios.name: Reject an incompatible required value column
given: schema metadata for AD_Public
all approved required column names
curr_market declared with an incompatible physical type
scenarios.when: the adapter validates the observed schema and the observable outcome is incompatible_physical_type followed by unsupported_schema before row conversion starts.
then: validation fails with incompatible_physical_type
row conversion does not begin
the failure is classified as unsupported_schema

requirements.title: Fingerprint observed schema deterministically
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST compute the schema fingerprint as SHA-256 over UTF-8 canonical JSON containing the parser contract version, exact table name, and all observed column descriptors sorted by exact column name, and MUST use the fingerprint only as provenance rather than as an allowlist.

scenarios.name: Fingerprint reordered compatible metadata
given: two compatible AD_Public descriptor collections containing identical descriptors in different input orders
one parser contract version
scenarios.when: the adapter fingerprints both collections and the observable outcomes are identical SHA-256 values while required-column compatibility is still evaluated independently.
then: both collections produce the same SHA-256 fingerprint
required-column compatibility is evaluated independently of the fingerprint

requirements.title: Create separate current and certified observations
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST emit the current value family and any consistently populated certified value family as separate immutable adapter-local observations carrying their own source family, source year, classification, exact source-column lineage, and provenance, and one family MUST NOT overwrite, merge with, relabel, suppress, or fill missing values for the other.

scenarios.name: Emit two observations from one physical row
given: a valid synthetic AD_Public row with curr_val_yr 2026
property_status Preliminary
a populated current value family
cert_val_yr 2025 and a populated certified value family
scenarios.when: the adapter converts the physical row and the observable outcomes are a preliminary current observation for 2026 and a separate certified observation for 2025 with family-specific lineage.
then: one preliminary current observation is emitted for 2026
one separate certified observation is emitted for 2025
matching values remain distinct records with family-specific lineage

requirements.title: Enforce identifier, year, status, null-family, and monetary rules
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST reject bool or out-of-range prop_id values, invalid geo_id text, unsupported property_status text, non-integral or out-of-range years, negative or oversized appraisal monetary values, and inconsistent certified-year/value null combinations, while preserving an allowed Access numeric null as None and every accepted Decimal exactly without rounding or exponent coercion.

scenarios.name: Reject a certified family without its year
given: a valid synthetic row with cert_val_yr null
at least one non-null certified monetary field
scenarios.when: the adapter validates certified-family consistency and the observable outcome is inconsistent_certified_family with neither the current nor certified observation from that physical row accepted.
then: row conversion fails with inconsistent_certified_family
no current or certified observation from the row is accepted

requirements.title: Preserve identifiers and physical row grain
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin adapter MUST preserve prop_id, geo_id, and every one-based physical source row as source facts, and MUST NOT declare either identifier to be an approved account key, equate the identifiers, deduplicate repeated rows, reconstruct owner associations, or infer an account roll-up.

scenarios.name: Preserve repeated source rows
given: two valid synthetic physical rows with the same prop_id and geo_id
different one-based physical row numbers
scenarios.when: the adapter converts both rows and the observable outcomes are retained records with distinct row provenance and no account-identity, deduplication, or roll-up assertion.
then: records for both physical rows are retained
each record carries its own physical-row provenance
no account identity, deduplication, or roll-up is asserted

requirements.title: Keep fixtures, records, and diagnostics privacy-safe
requirements.normative_rule: The Collin foundation MUST use only small independently authored synthetic or independently redistribution-safe fixtures, MUST NOT read or retain owner, mailing, DBA, or situs values, and MUST NOT place complete rows, arbitrary source values, protected identities, credentials, host-local paths, county artifacts, Access databases, archives, or production records in fixtures or diagnostics.

scenarios.name: Report an invalid geo_id safely
given: a synthetic row with an invalid geo_id
a one-based row number and schema fingerprint
scenarios.when: the adapter creates the failure diagnostic and the observable result contains only the stable code, approved field name, row number, and schema fingerprint, with no complete row or arbitrary value.
then: the diagnostic contains only bounded approved context
the diagnostic contains no complete row or arbitrary source value

requirements.title: Remain an adapter-local non-production foundation
requirements.normative_rule: The change MUST keep Collin, PACS, and Access vocabulary inside property_tax_adapters and MUST NOT add an Access runtime, network acquisition, production release-processing API, shared domain or application abstraction, service, DAG, persistence, migration, Bronze integration, Gold publication, workflow, infrastructure, deployment configuration, new dependency, or production-ready designation.

scenarios.name: Verify the implementation boundary
given: the completed candidate diff
the declared adapter, adapter-test, fixture, and source-documentation write scope
scenarios.when: repository path, dependency, architecture, artifact, and secret checks inspect the candidate and the observable outcomes show all changes within scope, unchanged domain and application packages, and no prohibited runtime or production integration.
then: every implementation path is within the declared write scope
property_tax_domain and property_tax_application remain unchanged
no prohibited runtime, persistence, orchestration, deployment, or dependency is introduced

risks: The measured 17-byte reader representation could be misrepresented as a universal raw Jet, Automation DECIMAL, OLE DB DB_NUMERIC, or generic Access wire format.
An implementation-derived fixture encoder could mirror an incorrect decoder and falsely validate word order, sign, scale, or precision handling.
Schema fingerprinting could be mistaken for compatibility approval rather than deterministic provenance.
Current and certified families could be combined in a way that erases release semantics or fabricates missing values.
Repeated prop_id rows could be prematurely treated as duplicates or approved account identities.
Fixtures, diagnostics, or documentation could accidentally include protected, county-derived, credential, or host-local data.
Synthetic fixtures establish a bounded contract but do not demonstrate compatibility, performance, or resource safety against a live production Access release.
security_privacy_considerations: Owner, mailing, DBA, and situs columns remain outside the typed projection and must not be read into records, fixtures, diagnostics, or extras.

Diagnostics are limited to a stable code, approved field or table name, one-based row number, and schema fingerprint; complete rows, arbitrary values, protected identities, credentials, and host-local paths are prohibited.
The implementation performs no network access, receives no production credentials, and adds no county artifact or Access runtime.
Only independently authored synthetic or independently redistribution-safe fixtures may be committed, with documented provenance and checksums.
Owner and mailing-address publication remains default-deny, and protected identities are never reconstructed.
migration_compatibility_concerns: No database or persisted schema change is authorized, so no data migration is required.
No backfill is authorized; future historical processing requires a separately accepted production release-processing contract.
Rollback consists of reverting or deleting the adapter-local decoder, records, tests, fixtures, and related documentation; no persisted or published data repair is needed.

The decoder contract is specific to the measured pure-Python reader representation; any future runtime must verify that representation against the independent vectors or introduce a versioned physical contract.
Additional schema columns may affect the fingerprint and produce extra_columns_present, but their values remain unread and required-column compatibility remains an independent gate.
No new dependency is approved; exact Decimal, canonical JSON, and SHA-256 behavior must use standard-library or already accepted facilities.
County Access databases, archives, production rows, and copied county values remain outside the repository and outside the project software-license grant.
The foundation does not establish live-release compatibility, production runtime compatibility, bounded streaming behavior, or production readiness.
non_goals: Live Collin discovery, probing, download, source contact, or network access.
ZIP handling, Access database extraction, runtime selection, containerization, benchmarking, or production compatibility certification.
Texas Open Data onboarding or transparent substitution for the measured Access contract.
Approval of prop_id or geo_id as an account key, owner-association deduplication, owner reconstruction, or account roll-up.
Shared vendor-neutral source-record, provenance, native-value, streaming, or production release-processing abstractions owned by Issue #43.
Changes to property_tax_domain, property_tax_application, services, DAGs, workflows, policies, providers, authentication, infrastructure, deployment, or production configuration.
Database migrations, Bronze persistence, Silver loading, Gold publication, API output, backfill, or production deployment.
Owner, mailing-address, DBA, situs, or protected-identity publication.
A production-ready designation for Collin or any other county adapter.
blocked_reasons: Implementation remains ineligible until an authorized maintainer merges the generated OpenSpec change; D1 through D4 are resolved only for draft generation and each requires human merge.

Defines the exact AD_Public table, privacy-minimized required columns, physical descriptors, nullability, name binding, extra-column behavior, schema fingerprint, and drift diagnostics.
Defines separate current and certified observations, accepted status classifications, mandatory family-specific provenance, immutability, and preservation of repeated physical rows.
Defines lexical and validation rules, stable bounded diagnostics, privacy limits, enforced implementation scope, task dependency ordering, and the Issue #43 boundary.

Records the accepted county-specific architecture, Collin dual-roll evidence, unresolved duplicate-row identity, exact-value concerns, and separation of Access from other county formats.
Documents source-onboarding boundaries, county-specific source contracts, fixture provenance expectations, and non-production foundation precedent.
Requires layout fingerprinting, fail-closed drift handling, small synthetic or redistribution-safe fixtures, documented checksums, and exclusion of full releases and protected owner data.
Defines the library dependency direction and requires source-specific translations to stop at the adapter boundary.

Requires maintained documentation changes to use appropriate links and pass make docs.

Provides Issue #18's source-onboarding objective, requested decoder and dual-observation scope, synthetic-fixture constraints, and prohibited production integration areas as untrusted requirements evidence.
Defines planning as structured read-only intent, restricts materialization to five OpenSpec artifacts, and requires human merge before implementation eligibility.
